executive_assessment.text: Named WASH hazard districts, Karamoja's dated water-access gap and Kampala informal settlements differentiate vulnerabilities without making FCV classifications.
Kawempe's water queues provide a source-stated tension mechanism. Household coping, policy perceptions and Karamoja mobility findings retain their sampling and regional limits.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2026 reports: The plan reports over 80% of populations in Katakwi, Otuke, Kitgum, Nwoya, Sembabule and Kalungu exposed to floods at least one metre deep.

Source dated 2026 reports: The plan reports over 80% population exposure to landslides in Bulambuli, Kapchorwa, Bukwo, Kween, Kisoro and Rubanda; over 60% of homes are exposed in five of these districts.
Source dated 2026 reports: In Karamoja, perennial surface water is scarce and valley dams cannot meet livestock needs; basic drinking-water access is 38%, compared with 97% in Kampala.
Source dated 2025-06 reports: KCCA identifies recurring floods in low-lying informal Bwaise, Katwe and Namuwongo; Nakawa, Makindye and Kawempe score highest on its division vulnerability index.
Source dated 2025-06 reports: KCCA links repeated 10-day dry spells in Kawempe to crop failures and unsafe-water reliance; long queues at communal water points are said to fuel social tension.

Source dated 2025-06 reports: KCCA reports flood-resistant housing and drainage among more consistently adopted household measures in Kawempe, Lubaga and Nakawa; stormwater retention adoption was low, especially in Central and Nakawa.
Source dated 2025-06 reports: In KCCA's 400-person household survey, 30% knew of climate policies and more than half considered them ineffective.

known_gaps.text: Opened sources describe climate mobility and vulnerability, but no country-specific climate-to-violence or armed-conflict link was inspected; no such pathway is asserted.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
The 2025 Karamoja Cluster article was available only as an abstract; it reports cross-border findings without Uganda-specific district attribution.

The 2026 WASH NAP's exposure indices rely substantially on the Office of the Prime Minister's 2019 hazard atlas; its local exposure percentages are not observed event-loss or climate-attribution estimates.
The FAO cattle-corridor endline factsheet repository link returned 403; the accessible release page omitted district names and substantive results.
No inspected source documented insecurity or violence preventing a named Ugandan climate-adaptation activity; that remains an evidence-search gap.
Main verified the Kawempe original narrative and the NAP/PreventionWeb summaries. Karamoja abstract findings remain cross-border; no district effect is invented.
OPM 2019 exposure mapping, UBOS 2020 water access, KCCA's purposive survey and 2019-cited risk narrative are different evidence types and vintages.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
